LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation, part of Strand 7 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do you use punctuation marks? 2. Which punctuation marks do you use when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify proper nouns such as names of people, places and features like mountains and rivers,

2. form sentences with peers using proper nouns,

3. write abbreviations of their school, names among others with peers and punctuate them correctly,

4. use punctuation cards to arrange or make coherent sentences and paragraphs collaboratively,

5. write well-punctuated sentences dictated by a teacher, peer or digital device,

6. make stickers with sentences punctuated with full stops and capital letters and stick them to a central place for everyone to see, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify proper nouns such as names of people, places and features like mountains and rivers,
2. form sentences with peers using proper nouns,
3. write abbreviations of their school, names among others with peers and punctuate them correctly,
4. use punctuation cards to arrange or make coherent sentences and paragraphs collaboratively,
5. write well-punctuated sentences dictated by a teacher, peer or digital device,
6. make stickers with sentences punctuated with full stops and capital letters and stick them to a central place for everyone to see, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as learners work together in groups forming sentences using

proper nouns.

• Digital Literacy: This is developed as the learner uses digital devices to type sentences and text.

Values:
• Unity: It is developed as the learner work together and make coherent sentences.

• Responsibility: It is promoted as the learner makes a list of abbreviations and punctuates them.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: This is enhanced as the learner work in group activities and make stickers with punctuated sentences.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of punctuation with their learning in Kiswahili.
